title: Standard Part (COTS catalog entry)
description: One entry of the keystone's standard-parts catalog (ASM-1 §4): a commercial off-the-shelf part an assembly document references with `source.type: standard`. An entry states FACTS only — the governing standard or datasheet with citation URLs, dimensions that each cite a source, optional parameters (e.g. an extrusion's cut length), and mating interfaces in the SEM-1 §2.3 shape (frame expressions over the entry's own parameters, polarity, a `size_key` from the `interface-sizes` vocabulary, rotational symmetry). Never datasheet prose and never CAD. A standard part is one rigid body; its model frame is stated in `frame_convention`. Which keys resolve, which expressions evaluate and whether every axis is a unit vector are rules of `hyperobjects_standard_parts`, not of this schema.

spec_version.description: Version of THIS catalog-entry contract the document is written against.

key.description: The catalog key an assembly writes (`source.key`) and the asset id derives from (`https://id.madfam.io/asset/standard/{key}`, ASM-1 §5). Kebab-case; a published name, so renaming one is a breaking change. The file is named `{key}.json`.

category.description: What kind of part this is — a grouping for readers and the catalog docs, not a mating rule.

status.description: `canonical` (default) — use it. `provisional` — real and usable, but a fact or a ruling on it is still open; `notes` says which.

name.description: The part's name in each language of the commons (RFC 0039).

description.description: One or two factual sentences in each language: what the part is and what it mates with. Not datasheet prose.

governing.description: What the entry's facts are governed by. `standard` — a published standard (cite it, or the manufacturer drawings that realise it when the standard is not freely published); `datasheet` — one manufacturer's part, at its datasheet; `class` — a commercial class many vendors build to (e.g. a 5-inch X frame), stated by facts every member shares and cited from several vendors, never a copy of any one design.

designation.description: The standard's identifier or the part number / class name the facts are read from.

source.description: Index into `sources` of the primary citation.

sources.description: The public citations behind the entry's facts. Every dimension and every parameter range that is a fact cites one by index.

frame_convention.description: The part's model frame in words (English): where the origin is, which way +x, +y and +z point, and which face or axis each interface frame sits on. Interface frames are written in this frame; an assembly places the part by them (ASM-1 §3.4).

dimensions.description: The part's dimensional and technical facts, by name. Every one cites a source.

parameters.description: Values an assembly may choose for one instance (ASM-1 §1 full injection: the default, overridden by the component's given value; out of range is an error, never clamped). Interface frame expressions may read them. A parameter is a choice, not a fact: its range cites a source when the range is the vendor's (an extrusion's stocked lengths), and says so in `note` when it is a convention.

interfaces.description: Where the part mates, in the SEM-1 §2.3 shape. `frame`, `polarity`, `size_key` and `symmetry` are all required here (the manifest makes them optional; a catalog entry exists to be mated). At least one, except for a `belt` (ASM-1 §9): a closed-loop belt has no end or seat to mate and appears only in an assembly's `paths[]`.

belt.description: ASM-1 §9 (v1.3). Category `belt` only, and required there: the belt facts a declared belt path (`paths[]` of an assembly) reads. Both cite a source.

pitch_line_differential.description: U: from the tooth tips' line to the pitch line.

teeth_side_offset.description: How far the pitch line sits from a smooth surface the TEETH run on (T + U). A path needs it to run this belt's teeth on a part with a `running_diameter`.

back_side_offset.description: How far the pitch line sits from a smooth surface the BACK runs on (B − T − U). A path needs it to run this belt's back on a part with a `running_diameter`.

loop_length.description: A closed-loop belt's pitch length. A path naming this belt must be closed; its computed length at home is reported beside this, and a difference above 0.5 mm (a convention) warns.

belt_engagement.description: ASM-1 §9 (v1.3). Where a belt wraps this part (a pulley, an idler or a bearing used as one), and the circle's centre and axis in the part's model frame. A toothed part states the cited `pitch_diameter` (the diameter the belt's pitch line runs on); a smooth part states the cited `running_diameter` (the surface the belt runs on), and a path adds the belt's pitch-line offset for the side that runs on it. Exactly one of the two. A belt path may pass only through components whose part declares this.

center.description: A point on the axis, in the belt's mid-plane, in the frame grammar over this entry's parameters.

axis.description: The pitch circle's axis: an EXACT unit vector.

parameters.description: The entry's parameter ids `center` and `axis` depend on.

plane_note.description: Where the mid-plane position along the axis comes from: a cited fact, or a convention labelled as one.

reviewState.description: `generated` — written in a drafting pass and not yet checked by a speaker of the language. `reviewed` — a named reviewer has read it and let it stand.

reviewStatus.description: The same review block a lexicon term carries: the overall state is the WORST facet, and `reviewed` needs a named reviewer.

source.description: A public citation a reader can follow — the same shape as a fabrication-vocabulary source. `supports` says which facts it backs, as facts, never quoted prose.

dimension.description: One fact, citing the entry's `sources` by index.

id.description: Identifier a frame expression reads; the same pattern as a manifest parameter id.

type.description: Always `number`: a standard part's choices are lengths and offsets.

source.description: Index into `sources` when the range is a vendor fact.

frameComponent.description: A number, or an expression string (at most 256 characters) over this entry's parameter ids and the interface's `let` names in the ASM-1 §1 frame grammar: numeric literals, + - * /, parentheses, min(), max(), abs(); and, from v1.1 (hyperobjects-spec >= 0.4.0), sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2(y, x) in DEGREES, sqrt, floor, ceil, round, the comparisons < <= > >= == != and iif(cond, a, b).

id.description: The interface id a mate names (`{component, interface}`); the cdg_interfaces id pattern.

geometry_type.description: The yantra4d interface geometry type. Must equal the `geometry_type` of the `size_key`'s interface-sizes entry.

size_key.description: An `interface-sizes` vocabulary key. Always a literal here: a standard part has no select parameter to map from.

polarity.description: Which side of the pair this is (catalog convention, docs/STANDARD_PARTS.md): `female` receives — a tapped or plain hole a fastener's thread or a partner's stud enters, a bore, a slot, a bay; `male` inserts or carries the fastener head — a shaft, a stud or standoff, a body that goes into a bay or pocket, the clearance-hole side a screw passes through into a female partner. `neutral` for face-to-face contact with no inserting side.

symmetry.description: Rotational symmetry order about `normal`: 0 continuous, 1 none, else the number of equivalent orientations.

let.description: Named derived numbers this interface's frame may read (ASM-1 v1.1; needs hyperobjects-spec >= 0.4.0): name → expression in the frame grammar over the entry's parameters and the block's other names, evaluated in dependency order. A standard part has no select, so a catalog `let` is always an expression.

frame.description: Where the interface sits, in mm, in the part's model frame (`frame_convention`) at the resolved parameters. `normal` points from the feature toward where the mating partner sits; `x_axis` is the in-plane reference direction. Both are required to be EXACT unit vectors, orthogonal, at the parameter defaults — a catalog entry carries no normalisation slack. `part`, when written, must equal the entry key (a standard part is one rigid body).

travel.description: ASM-1 §9 (v1.4). How far an assembly mate's `offset` may slide this interface along one axis of its own frame: `range` is [lower, upper] in mm, in the frame grammar over the entry's parameters (list them in `parameters`). A slot station on an extrusion travels the slot's run.

parameters.description: The entry's parameter ids this interface's frame depends on.
